Repository: encode/httpx
Language: Python

Redundant `boundary` if files/data is empty
If you try to send a post request with empty data and files — you will create a body with one `--boundary--` string, which can break the server.

It's because httpx create MultipartStream for `data={}, files={}`:
https://github.com/encode/httpx/blob/a82adcc933345c6b8cb1623b031eb85723e7665b/httpx/_content_streams.py#L332-L334

And this MultipartStream doesn't have special behavior for empty data/files:
https://github.com/encode/httpx/blob/a82adcc933345c6b8cb1623b031eb85723e7665b/httpx/_content_streams.py#L277-L283

Reproducible example:

```
from httpx.content_streams import encode

stream = encode(data={}, files={}, boundary=b"+++")
print(b"".join([part for part in stream]))
# b'--+++--\r\n'
```

I see two ways to solve it:
1. Check files not only for None but also for emptiness in `_content_streams.decode`
2. Check the count of fields in `MultipartStream.__init__` and doesn't write anything if fields are empty.

I already opened PR (#861) with a test example. If someone tells me which of these options is better, I will be happy to implement it  🙌

Language: Python

Redundant `boundary` if files/data is empty
If you try to send a post request with empty data and files — you will create a body with one `--boundary--` string, which can break the server.

It's because httpx create MultipartStream for `data={}, files={}`:
https://github.com/encode/httpx/blob/a82adcc933345c6b8cb1623b031eb85723e7665b/httpx/_content_streams.py#L332-L334

And this MultipartStream doesn't have special behavior for empty data/files:
https://github.com/encode/httpx/blob/a82adcc933345c6b8cb1623b031eb85723e7665b/httpx/_content_streams.py#L277-L283

Reproducible example:

```
from httpx.content_streams import encode

stream = encode(data={}, files={}, boundary=b"+++")
print(b"".join([part for part in stream]))
# b'--+++--\r\n'
```

I see two ways to solve it:
1. Check files not only for None but also for emptiness in `_content_streams.decode`
2. Check the count of fields in `MultipartStream.__init__` and doesn't write anything if fields are empty.

I already opened PR (#861) with a test example. If someone tells me which of these options is better, I will be happy to implement it  🙌

item.text: The extra boundary comes from one branch in `encode`: an empty `files` dict still selects multipart when `data` is a dict. I’ll treat empty `files` as absent there, so populated `data` uses form encoding and empty `data` produces an empty body.

import pytest

import httpx


def test_request_repr():
    request = httpx.Request("GET", "http://example.org")
    assert repr(request) == "<Request('GET', 'http://example.org')>"


def test_no_content():
    request = httpx.Request("GET", "http://example.org")
    assert "Content-Length" not in request.headers


def test_content_length_header():
    request = httpx.Request("POST", "http://example.org", data=b"test 123")
    assert request.headers["Content-Length"] == "8"


def test_url_encoded_data():
    request = httpx.Request("POST", "http://example.org", data={"test": "123"})
    request.read()

    assert request.headers["Content-Type"] == "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"
    assert request.content == b"test=123"


def test_json_encoded_data():
    request = httpx.Request("POST", "http://example.org", json={"test": 123})
    request.read()

    assert request.headers["Content-Type"] == "application/json"
    assert request.content == b'{"test": 123}'


def test_read_and_stream_data():
    # Ensure a request may still be streamed if it has been read.
    # Needed for cases such as authentication classes that read the request body.
    request = httpx.Request("POST", "http://example.org", json={"test": 123})
    request.read()
    content = b"".join([part for part in request.stream])
    assert content == request.content


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_aread_and_stream_data():
    # Ensure a request may still be streamed if it has been read.
    # Needed for cases such as authentication classes that read the request body.
    request = httpx.Request("POST", "http://example.org", json={"test": 123})
    await request.aread()
    content = b"".join([part async for part in request.stream])
    assert content == request.content
